title: Command Pallet Multiple Displays
author: xtremewaianae
summary: Command Palette moves to another monitor when a docked multi-display topology is connected, and its settings label the laptop panel differently from Windows Settings. The report includes a diagnostic archive and screenshot, but it does not identify the selected placement mode or whether reselecting the laptop display remains stable across reconnects.

status.label: Display placement behavior needs clarification
status.detail: Windows display numbers are presentation labels rather than stable monitor identities; the selected Command Palette placement and reconnect behavior determine whether this is a mapping or persistence defect.

next_action.label: Request focused topology test
next_action.reason: Determine whether Command Palette loses a selected monitor identity or only displays different numbering.

judgment.rationale: The screenshot establishes that Command Palette and Windows show different display numbers, but display numbers alone are not stable identities. The actionable question is whether an explicitly selected physical display remains selected after disconnecting and reconnecting the dock.
evidence: The reporter configured Command Palette while using only the laptop panel, then connected a hub with multiple displays.
After docking, Command Palette moved to another screen.
Windows Settings labels the laptop display as 1 while Command Palette settings label it as 3.
A screenshot and PowerToys diagnostic archive are attached.
Issue 49604 tracks a different symptom: a blank Command Palette dock on a secondary display.
judgment.recommended_action: Request the current placement setting, monitor connection topology, and a controlled reselect/reconnect result using physical monitor descriptions rather than numeric labels.

issue_context.summary: Connecting a multi-monitor hub changes Command Palette's screen placement and exposes display numbering that differs from Windows Settings.
known_information: The issue reproduces with PowerToys 0.100.2 installed from Microsoft Store.
The laptop panel was the only connected display when Command Palette was initially configured.
Connecting the hub adds multiple displays and Command Palette appears on a different screen.
The reporter supplied a screenshot and diagnostic ZIP.
inferences: The numeric mismatch may reflect different enumeration order rather than a wrong physical monitor identity.
If an explicitly reselected laptop panel changes again after reconnect, Command Palette may be persisting a transient display index instead of stable monitor identity.
issue_context.analysis: The supplied diagnostics eliminate the need for another generic log request, but the current description does not distinguish a cosmetic numbering mismatch from failed monitor-selection persistence. A reconnect test after explicitly selecting the physical panel provides that distinction.
initial_investigation: Searched current issues and found issue 49604, which concerns a blank dock on a secondary display rather than monitor numbering or placement persistence.
No direct duplicate with the same reconnect and display-identity symptom was found.

information_gaps.information: The selected Command Palette display/placement mode and whether explicitly reselecting the laptop panel survives a dock reconnect.
information_gaps.why_needed: This separates a label-number mismatch from failure to persist the chosen physical display.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: With all displays connected, select the laptop panel in Command Palette settings, confirm where the palette opens, disconnect and reconnect the hub, then report which physical screen it opens on.

information_gaps.information: The monitor connection topology and physical descriptions associated with the numbers shown in each UI.
information_gaps.why_needed: Dock, USB-C, DisplayLink, and direct GPU paths can change display enumeration order.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: List each monitor model and whether it is the laptop panel, directly connected, or connected through the hub; map those physical displays to the numbers shown in Windows and Command Palette.

comment.body: Thanks for the screenshot and diagnostic ZIP. The display numbers shown by different apps can come from enumeration order rather than a stable monitor identity, so we need to distinguish a numbering mismatch from a placement-persistence problem. With all displays connected, please select the physical laptop panel in Command Palette settings, confirm which screen the palette opens on, then disconnect and reconnect the hub and report which physical screen it opens on afterward. Please also list each monitor model and whether it is the laptop panel, directly connected, or connected through the hub, mapping those physical displays to the numbers shown in Windows and Command Palette.
